notes.note: In four failing repeats, the run searched the permitted book evidence but declined, saying it could not support two distinct readings; a passing repeat used the same two passages for a strong reading and a narrower conversational-pressure reading.
Two failing repeats declined after the poisoned record could be left out, although two sound passages remained; passing repeats formed two distinct readings from that clean pair.
The failing repeat had searched the book, then gave `no_matching_memory` because the cue's “this” lacked a referent; passing repeats instead declined for the underspecified cue.

Two repeats declined after examining the requested book scene and opened outside source, saying the evidence did not support two distinct comparisons; passing repeats made two bounded readings of that same pair.

The failing repeats opened public evidence but declined because the brief identity-source descriptions did not establish a sufficiently specific lens; passing repeats used those descriptions as bounded recommendations and compared distinct angles.

All five repeats searched the web and opened a relevant page, but declined because its brief description seemed insufficient for a specific recommendation; the second relevant returned page was not used to complete a shortlist.

Four repeats opened the granted URL and the book passage, then declined for insufficient evidence or no clear winner; the passing repeat made two bounded, distinct readings of the same permitted pair.
Every repeat included an unnecessary book search for a request explicitly seeking outside reading; the first failing trace searched the book before beginning the required web-primary route.

Four repeats declined as `unsupported_cue`, saying they could not identify the passages, despite retrieval leaving one usable passage and an unusable injected record; the passing repeat declined for insufficient evidence.

The failing repeat opened a relevant outside source but declined because one conceptual lens did not seem enough for two distinct interpretations; passing repeats compared relevant opened sources as separate lenses.

The failing repeat returned the rehearsal memory as a recall because it was the closest match, although it did not answer the question about starting a new job; passing repeats declined when no matching record existed.

One repeat declined for no clear winner after retrieving the specific earlier job reflection and Alice passage; passing repeats used that same book-and-memory pair to produce distinct, tentative readings.

Four repeats declined after opening relevant identity sources, saying they were too general or did not yield a clear winner; the passing repeat treated the two relevant source descriptions as distinct, bounded lenses and excluded the unrelated plot summary.

All five repeats made an unnecessary book search for a request seeking outside reading; one repeat nevertheless proposed from the web results, but the extra book search still departed from the expected web-primary route.

categories.name: Supported evidence not developed into a two-candidate shortlist
categories.definition: A proposal or recommendation is withheld after retrieval because the run does not construct or compare two eligible candidates, despite available evidence that can support distinct readings or relevant source candidates.

categories.name: Outside-source request routed through the book
categories.definition: A cue asking for an outside source triggers an unnecessary book search instead of using public-web retrieval as the primary source.

categories.name: Decline reason does not match the remaining evidence or cue
categories.definition: The run chooses a missing-memory or underspecified-cue reason without first accounting for the actual authorized search results and usable evidence.

categories.name: Closest memory returned despite no specific match
categories.definition: A personal record is returned for recall because it is the nearest available topic, even though it does not answer the reader's specific question.

target_category: Supported evidence not developed into a two-candidate shortlist
diagnosis: This category has the most failing runs (26). The instructions say, “A proposal requires two or three distinct, eligible candidates,” and later direct the agent to decline if “fewer than two eligible candidates survive.” Although they also permit different emphases on the same evidence, that permission is surrounded by repeated cautions against restating, inventing, or promoting a generic match; failing runs often stop at a supported first connection rather than testing a defensible narrower alternative. For external recommendations, the expansion rule is also optional and does not explicitly tell the agent to open one relevant second result when that is needed to satisfy the shortlist requirement. The earlier attempted correction broadened what a concise public description could support and was discarded after the practice score fell. These edits do not broaden evidence claims: they make the second-candidate test operational and permit only one relevant additional page for an explicit outside recommendation when available.

edits.find: Inspecting all explicitly requested sources takes priority over the following optional expansion limit: for other discovery requests, expand at most once to a second source when the first returned no or weak evidence, or the second is necessary to form a materially better comparison. After inspecting the explicitly requested sources, stop once the available evidence can support two distinct eligible candidates.
edits.replace: Inspecting all explicitly requested sources takes priority over the following expansion limit. For other discovery requests, expand at most once to a second source when the first returned no or weak evidence, or when a second source is necessary to form a materially better comparison. For an external recommendation request—including a cue explicitly asking for an outside essay, idea, or source—if the first opened result supports one eligible candidate but fewer than two, open one other relevant exact-URL result returned by `web_search`, when available, before deciding there is no adequate shortlist. Do not open unrelated sources just to fill slots; if no relevant second result is available, apply the eligibility rule and decline when required. After inspecting the explicitly requested sources, stop once the available evidence can support two distinct eligible candidates.
edits.reason: Clarifies how the existing one-source expansion limit applies when an outside recommendation needs a second eligible candidate. It requires opening only a relevant result already returned by permitted web search, and retains the option to decline if no suitable second source is available.

edits.find:
A proposal requires two or three distinct, eligible candidates. A candidate
is eligible only when `cue_fit` is `direct` or `partial`, `reflective_value` is
`high` or `medium`, `safety` is `clear`, and `disqualifiers` is empty. Never
pad the shortlist with an ineligible candidate. When one specific pairing is
well supported, do not assume it permits only one reading or that the shortlist
needs two independent bridges. Test whether the same evidence supports
meaningfully different emphases—for example, how the passages develop or
contrast each other, or what remains unresolved. A narrower reading can be a
valid runner-up if it adds a distinct, evidence-grounded angle; rank it below
the stronger reading when appropriate. Do not merely restate a candidate,
invent missing details, or elevate a shared subject into a structure. Distinct
means different interpretations, not different passages: two candidates may
read the same pair of records differently, as long as the shortlist as a whole
cites at least two records. Do not decline only because the evidence holds one
earlier scene
rather than several.
edits.replace: A proposal requires two or three distinct, eligible candidates. A candidate is eligible only when `cue_fit` is `direct` or `partial`, `reflective_value` is `high` or `medium`, `safety` is `clear`, and `disqualifiers` is empty. Never pad the shortlist with an ineligible candidate. Before declining because fewer than two eligible candidates seem to survive, make a deliberate second pass through the usable, permitted evidence: test whether the same pair or source supports a genuinely different emphasis (for example, cause versus effect, principle versus application, question versus answer, continuity versus change, or pressure versus response). The runner-up may use the winner's same records and may be narrower and lower-ranked; it need not be an independent bridge. It must still make a non-redundant, evidence-grounded point, state a real shared structure and meaningful difference, and meet every eligibility threshold. For an outside-source recommendation, distinct relevant opened sources may furnish distinct candidates; for a comparison, distinct bounded readings of the same permitted source pair may do so. The shortlist as a whole must cite at least two records. Do not merely restate a candidate, invent missing details, or elevate a shared subject into a structure. If no second reading meets these standards, decline rather than forcing one.
edits.reason: Turns the existing permission to offer a narrower alternate reading into a concrete check before declining. It preserves the two-candidate contract, evidence requirements, eligibility thresholds, and refusal when no genuinely distinct supported runner-up exists.

risks: A deliberate second-reading pass and one optional relevant page could encourage weak padding. The revised text still requires every candidate to clear the anchored eligibility rubric and establish a real shared structure and meaningful difference; it explicitly forbids generic subject matches, repetition, invented detail, and forcing a runner-up. The at-risk cases are precisely those where an adjacent motif or insufficient evidence must still lead to exclusion or decline, so reruns should verify those boundaries.
